claims.object_text: predominant expression in cerebellar Purkinje cells
claims.quote: Because cerebellar Purkinje cells (PCs) predominantly, if not exclusively, express one isoform of this family, α2δ-2 (Cacna2d2),

claims.object_text: altered climbing fiber-evoked complex spike generation

claims.object_text: increased amplitude and faster decay of CF-evoked EPSCs
claims.quote: as well as increased amplitude and faster decay of CF-evoked EPSCs.

claims.object_text: proximal localization of CF terminals on PC dendrites
claims.quote: CF terminals in the KO were localized more proximally on PC dendrites, as indicated by VGLUT2+ immunoreactive puncta,

claims.object_text: increased EPSC amplitude partly attributed to more proximal CF terminal location (computational modeling)
claims.quote: and computational modeling demonstrated that the increased EPSC amplitude can be partly attributed to the more proximal location of CF terminals.

claims.object_text: increased multivesicular transmission with greater sustained responses during repetitive stimulation despite reduced probability of release
claims.quote: In addition, CFs in KO mice exhibited increased multivesicular transmission, corresponding to greater sustained responses during repetitive stimulation, despite a reduction in the measured probability of release.

claims.object_text: twice as many vesicle release sites in mutant CF terminals
claims.quote: Electron microscopy demonstrated that mutant CF terminals had twice as many vesicle release sites,

claims.object_text: increased glutamate reuptake producing faster decay kinetics resulting in unchanged charge transfer
claims.quote: the charge transfer was the same as wild-type as a result of increased glutamate reuptake, producing faster decay kinetics.

claims.object_text: altered complex spike responses degrade information transfer and likely contribute to ataxia in Cacna2d2 KO mice
claims.quote: Together, the larger, faster EPSCs in the KO explain the altered complex spike responses, which degrade information transfer from PCs and likely contribute to ataxia in Cacna2d2 KO mice.
